about: Formal readings of the dev half of the outside benchmark (items.jsonl, split in FROZEN.md). One entry per dev item, in items.jsonl order. Each expected field (alone, with_hypotheses) is covered either by readings (a spec in specs/ plus named claims of physverify/schemes/claims.py) or by one `unformalized` entry with reasons from the taxonomy in README.md. Expected values are read from items.jsonl, never copied here. Run: uv run python benchmark/outside/run_dev.py [--write]; field meanings are in its docstring.

readings.reading: where f' != 0, the WENO schemes of Liu, Osher and Chan (smoothness measurement (2.18)) built from the r-th order ENO stencils are of order at least r + 1, for r = 2 and r = 3, eps negligible
readings.narrowing: r = 2 and r = 3, the cases the source writes out (Tables 1-2); for r = 2, (2.18) is (f[j+k-1, 1])^2, the same as (2.19), and for r = 3 it is (2.20). One split flux component, the order as the truncation error of (f^_{j+1/2} - f^_{j-1/2})/dx at one grid point, eps -> 0 written eps = 0 (the item's hypothesis), as for jiang_shu_1995_weno:05. '(r+1)th order accurate' read as 'at least r + 1', its usual sense; for r = 3 the leading order is in fact 5 (see jiang_shu_1995_weno:02, with hypotheses), which this reading does not need
readings.found_by: the reconstruction v3 survey; the checker is unchanged (reconstruction_order_p as in v2)

unformalized.note: as jiang_shu_1995_weno:02 and :05 alone: the bare sentence's truth at critical points depends on how eps scales with dx. Run once, not stored: with eps = 0 (or eps = dx^4) and n_cp = 1, reconstruction_order_p on the flux difference is REFUTED for p = r + 1 (r = 3: leading order 2, the face value alone order 3, the source's 'only 3rd order'; r = 2: order 1); with eps = 10^-6 fixed it is VERIFIED at n_cp = 1. The FALSE value rests on the eps << IS_k family, so a reading in that family alone would be the family that makes the checker match (team rule for eps-family choices). Before reconstruction v3 this field was `reconstruction`

the truth of the bare sentence depends on how eps scales with dx, and the sentence does not fix it. Jiang and Shu define eps as a fixed positive constant (p. 6, after (2.16): 'we will take eps = 10^-6') but derive the order with eps left out ((2.17), (3.8)-(3.9)), and on p. 7 they explain fixed-eps convergence on fine grids as an artefact of IS_k << eps. FALSE rests on the eps << IS_k family (the justification: 'when eps does not dominate the indicators'). Run once, not stored: with eps = 0 (or eps = dx^4), reconstruction_order_p on the flux difference at n_cp = 1 is REFUTED for p = 5 (leading order 3); with eps = 10^-6 fixed it is VERIFIED at n_cp = 1, and VERIFIED would need every n_cp, so that reading could reach only NOT_REFUTED. A reading in the eps << IS_k family alone would be the family that makes the checker match, and one in the fixed-eps family is an instance whose truth differs from the expected value (README, Readings), so the field is left unformalised (team rule for eps-family choices)

the clause 'instead of the 4th order with the original smoothness measurement' decides the field, and its reading is a judgment call. Run once, not stored: with eps -> 0 (the item's hypothesis, written eps = 0) and f' != 0, reconstruction_order_p on the flux difference is VERIFIED for p = 5 with the new measurement (3.2)-(3.4) and ALSO VERIFIED for p = 5 with the original one (2.20) (leading order 5; cross-checked by direct exact evaluation, error/dx^4 -> 0). The O(h) terms of (2.23)-(2.25) are -2, 0, +2 times f''h/f', linear in k, and such weight errors cancel against the candidate errors at O(h^4); the source's 'can only give 4th order' (p. 7) rests on the sufficient condition (2.14) only. Read as 'the original gives 4th and not 5th order' the sentence is false and the expected TRUE would score WRONG; read as 'at least 4th' it is VERIFIED. Neither is forced by the text, so the field is left unformalised (see ERRATA_PROPOSED.md)
convergence of every WENO scheme with Runge-Kutta time stepping
pointwise convergence theorem for WENO with RK of order n >= max(r, 3), d dimensions

readings.reading: where f' != 0, the WENO schemes with the new measurement are (2r-1)th order for r = 2 and r = 3, eps negligible
readings.narrowing: one split flux component: v_k = f^+_{j+k} and the reconstruction f^_{j+1/2} (f^- is its mirror image); order = truncation error of the spatial operator (f^_{j+1/2} - f^_{j-1/2})/dx against f^+(u(x))_x at one grid point x_j, with both reconstructions expanded about x_j; eps family: eps -> 0, written eps = 0 (with f' != 0 every IS_k is (f' dx)^2 (1 + O(dx)) > 0, so the weights are defined). This is a family choice, and the item's hypotheses make it: 'eps treated as negligible in the order analysis' (pp. 6-9). The sufficient condition (2.17), IS_k = D(1 + O(h^{r-1})), and (3.8) only bear on the weights when eps is negligible against IS_k; with eps fixed the weights tend to C_k whatever IS_k is (p. 7: 'on fine grids, since the smoothness measurements IS_k for all k are relatively smaller than the non-zero constant eps in (2.16), the weights become close to the optimal weights'); 'at least for r = 2, 3' read as the two cases r = 2, 3

formalization.bridge: '(k+1)-th order accurate limiter' read as the bound max_I |p~ - p| <= C_k max_I dist(p, [m, M]) with C_k depending on k only: dist(p(y), [m, M]) <= |p(y) - u(y)| for every u with values in [m, M], so max |p~ - u| <= (1 + C_k) max |p - u| = O(dx^(k+1)) when p is (k+1)-th order accurate (the accuracy of p is part of the notion, as the item's justification says); both sides are unchanged by the affine map of I_j to y in [-1/2, 1/2], so C_k does not depend on dx
